 By TSN.ca Staff Opens in new window Published:   November 20, 2026 at 6:07p.m. EST 
 The Vancouver Canucks have traded forward Max Sasson to the New York Rangers for a fourth-round draft pick in the 2029 NHL Draft, the teams announced on Friday.
 Sasson, 26, has five goals and eight points in 24 games with the Canucks this season.
 The 6-foot-1 centre is on the first season of a two-year, $2 million contract that carries an annual cap hit of $1 million. He is scheduled to become an unrestricted free agent after the 2027-28 campaign.
 Originally signed as an undrafted free agent by the Canucks in 2023, Sasson has 21 goals and 34 points in 119 career games in Vancouver.
 He also helped the AHL’s Abbotsford Canucks to a Calder Cup championship in 2025, registering five goals and 14 points during their playoff run.
 The Birmingham, Mich., native represented the United States at the 2026 World Hockey Championship, recording a goal and two points in a sixth-place finish.
 Sasson is joining a Rangers team that sits third in the Metropolitan Division with a 13-8-1 record, three points behind the second place New Jersey Devils .
 Vancouver is in last place in the NHL with a 5-18-1 record.
